newsitem.title: PORTUGAL: Public opinion threatens EMU start - Lamfalussy.
newsitem.headline: Public opinion threatens EMU start - Lamfalussy.

text.p: European Monetary Institute (EMI) president Alexandre Lamfalussy was quoted as saying on Monday that public opinion in some countries was a threat to the start of Economic and Monetary Union (EMU).

"I am worried about public opinion in various countries. As monetary union approaches, people are beginning to see how it will affect their lives," Lamfalussy told Diario de Noticias newspaper in an interview.
"Why give up your own currency if it is in good shape?" added Lamfalussy, who visited Lisbon last week to attend 150th anniversary celebrations of the Bank of Portugal.

"I think also that it is a shame that all the advantages of the euro (single currency) have not been explained in various countries," said Lamfalussy, the head of what will eventually become the European Union's central bank.
Lamfalussy also said he was concerned about global economic uncertainties ahead of the launch of the euro on January 1 1999.
